item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Florida Panthers had a rough start to their road schedule this season. It is not getting any easier. Florida opens up a three-game trip this afternoon in Washington and, once it wraps up in Columbus on Tuesday, the Panthers will have played 13 of their first 19 away from Sunrise. If the season ended today, Florida would squeak into a wild-card playoff spot. Yet, of Florida’s 16 games played to date, only four have been against teams currently in a playoff position: Carolina (OT win), Seattle (W), Ottawa (L), and Minnesota (L). The four wins in the last five games – two against Chicago and two against Winnipeg – came against teams playing well under .500 hockey. Sandwiched within those wins was a loss to Detroit minus star Dylan Larkin . Their losses to an improved Ottawa team and a struggling Pittsburgh team on the last road trip were lopsided affairs. Atlantic Division leader Boston will be the toughest opponent in the upcoming three-game journey, but Washington and Columbus cannot be ignored. Washington and Boston are on successive afternoons which is a break of sorts because it allows them to arrive in Boston at a reasonable hour and get a full night’s rest. One guy who appreciates the matinees is Niko Mikkola . “It’s prime time in Finland so everybody – friends and family – can watch it a little bit easier,’’ he said before Friday’s flight. “I really like those games.” The upcoming schedule is so tight that it leaves little time between games for rest or practice. Paul Maurice put the Panthers to work on Friday morning, perhaps because their next practice is not “until the 19th of November” he said. That is a whopping thirteen days between practices. Lineup adjustments will have to be rehearsed at the morning pregame skates. For today, Maurice will probably not make any lineup changes after the Chicago win. “Not planned as of now,’’ he said. “I’ve got a couple of game-timers. We’ll see.” Boston is now 12-4-1 and is atop the Atlantic Division. David Pastrnak has eight goals and 22 points in 17 games. He has always performed well against Florida. Alex Ovechkin may no longer be the player we knew but the Caps have Dylan Strome and newly acquired Jordan Kyrou and Alex Tuch all enjoying good starts this season. item.description: Patriots Face Important Mack Hollins Decision Before Packers Game originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots have a significant roster decision to make Saturday, and the outcome could directly affect Drake Maye's options against the Green Bay Packers. Veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins returned to practice this week after spending time on injured reserve with a calf injury. New England must activate Hollins to its 53-man roster by 4 p.m. ET Saturday if it wants him available for Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium. The timing matters because the Patriots already have ruled out A.J. Brown with ankle and knee injuries. Tight end Hunter Henry also remains questionable with a foot injury, leaving New England facing the possibility of playing without two of Maye's most important receiving options. Hollins Could Fill A Significant Void Before his injury, Hollins had emerged as a dependable part of New England's passing attack. He led the team with 15 receptions and 209 receiving yards through the first four weeks, providing Maye with an experienced target capable of working across different areas of the field. item.title: ‘Beyond parody’: Fox News can’t stop talking about Sophie Cunningham after Republican midterm losses
item.description: Credit: Fox News, Reuters Images Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections, with Democrats taking control of both the House and the Senate. But if you’ve been watching Fox News since then, you might have noticed that one of its favorite topics has been a WNBA player. The network has run multiple segments on Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham in the days since the election, including several built around a post she shared on social media. Political journalist Aaron Rupar called the coverage “beyond parody.” Fox News and Sophie Cunningham Fox News has been fixated on Cunningham ever since she told ESPN in July that she wants to “protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.” The network ran at least 206 WNBA segments over the summer, according to a Media Matters for America report, via Awful Announcing , with many of them focused on anti-trans rhetoric after her interview. Cunningham has insisted that her own political views are “right in the middle.” But she has become a hero for many conservatives, and Fox didn’t waste any time turning back to her after Republicans’ losses on Tuesday. On Wednesday morning, Fox & Friends co-host Ainsley Earhardt and contributor Brett Cooper spent a segment gushing over Cunningham instead of breaking down the election results. “You see Sophie Cunningham, who is defending women’s sports and fairness in women’s sports, and she has so many followers. She has gained more followers than any other of the top 49 WNBA players combined,” Earhardt said. “Well, I think that politics aside, Sophie Cunningham is hot, and she’s funny,” Cooper responded. “I think that being an attractive woman and actually being a joyful person, loving your sport, loving what you do, loving the opportunities that are in front of you, she’s not biting the hand that feeds her.” That was one of four Fox shows that praised Cunningham on Wednesday, according to Awful Announcing . Later that day, Cunningham shared a lengthy post on her Instagram story that was written by supplement company CEO Andy Frisella, arguing that “politics is downstream of culture.” ‘Beyond parody’ The coverage continued on Friday morning, when Fox & Friends aired two more segments on Cunningham’s post. Rupar, who tracks Fox News coverage closely, shared clips of both. “‘This message isn’t cope’ — you can’t make it up — Fox & Friends is coping with Republicans’ historic midterm destruction by having daily Sophie Cunningham segments, including treating her social media posts like they are news. Sophie 2028!” Rupar wrote on Bluesky . “Beyond parody — Fox & Friends this morning had not one BUT TWO lengthy Sophie Cunningham segments based on her cliche-packed social media post that was vaguely meant to cheer up conservatives,” he added . item.title: Nick Saban says there’s been a change in college football that he hates to see
item.description: Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images With the proposed changes to the College Football Playoff gathering momentum, Nick Saban has highlighted one problem he has with the plan. No head coach knows as much about winning championships in collegiate football as Nick Saban. The legendary head coach of the Alabama Crimson Tide won seven national championships during his career, and also claimed 11 SEC championships to boot. As the CFP (College Football Playoff) gets closer to a larger bracket, one of the discussed sacrifices to make that happen would be the conference championship games. As someone who experienced so much success in those games, Saban has now given his verdict on the situation. Nick Saban explains why he doesn’t want the conference championship games to go An expanded College Football Playoff has been in discussions for a long time. And one of the arguments against the conference championship games is that the extra game has become an unnecessary risk, potentially damaging a team’s playoff chances. Saban doesn’t agree though, and he made his feelings on the matter quite clear during a recent appearance on the New Heights podcast. “But what you’re giving up, which is what I hate to see is, you know, the SEC Championship game, playing in the SEC Championship was a big thing to our players. It was a big thing to our fans. It was a tradition and it was a great venue,” the legendary coach said. “I mean, there’s only two teams that can play in the National Championship, but more teams can play in those kind of championship games. And, you know, there’s a lot of pride in winning the Conference Championship. And, you know, we played in those games. “I mean, we’re one, Florida’s two, Florida’s one, we’re two, Georgia’s three, we’re one. I mean, it was a great game and great players love that. And we’re going to give that up to have an extra game where the 24th team is going to play the ninth best team. “I mean, if we had just put the right 12 teams in and didn’t go through all the political BS that we went through so we could have a 12-team playoff and end up putting a couple teams in, it shouldn’t be in, and then some other teams that should have been in didn’t get in, that was a good tournament.” Saban makes some valid points here, especially considering that having just one national championship means that a lot of teams will lose out on the experience of the smaller but still meaningful wins. It remains to be seen if his speaking out on the situation will actually change anything. item.title: Onyx Nnani turns in a pair of double-digit performances to start Bryant career
item.description: LAUSANNE, SWITZERLAND - JULY 01: Onyx Nnani of Canada drives to the basket the FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2025 Group B game between Germany v Canada at Lausanne Arena on July 01, 2025 in Lausanne, Switzerland. (Photo by Vianney Thibaut/FIBA via Getty Images) | FIBA via Getty Images Onyx Nnani played just one game as freshman for coach Bryan Hodgson at South Florida last year but has burst onto the scene with Bryant this week with back-to-back career-high 13-point games for the Bulldogs. The 20-year-old from Edmonton, Alberta, native already has an accomplished career. Nnani had the opportunity to travel to Switzerland last year for the FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup. In seven games played for his home nation, Nnani averaged 7.7 points and five rebounds per game with his strongest performance coming against Slovenia in which he recorded 10 points and 10 rebounds for the double-double. His ability to produce on a high stage has long been recognized. “Onyx is the kind of long wing who can grow into a modern forward,” one Canadian talent evaluator said during his time in prep school. The power forward averaged 24.3 points per game and 9.2 rebounds per game in his senior year of prep school. His ability to produce and to lead his squad garnered the attention of Hodgson, who was at Arkansas State at the time. Hodgson brought Nnani with him to South Florida. “Onyx was recruited at the highest level of college basketball and brings a skill set and versatility, combined with great size and length to have an immediate impact on our program,” Hodgson said when he initially signed Nnani to ASU . As a freshman, Nnani only appeared in one game for the Bulls. However, the former Canadian National Team forward is proving he is capable of living up to the high expectations set for him after averaging 22.5 points throughout the entirety of his prep school career. In his first two starts for Jamion Christian’s Bulldogs, the 6-foot-9 big put up 13 points and seven rebounds in a season-opening win over Siena. He followed it up with another 13 points to go with four boards in a loss to Quinnipiac. Nnani has shot a combined 8-for-23 from the floor and 8-of-12 at the free-throw line. Coming off a redshirt year, Nnani is on pace to average almost double his points from his seven World Cup games. As he finds his place in this new Bulldogs squad, he fits the mold of what Christian is building in Smithfield. “Our vision is built on three pillars: collective size, elite shooting, and versatile playmaking,” Christian said . Nnani will look to continue his double-digit scoring ways when the Bulldogs host the Fairfield Stags in the America East-Metro Challenge Sunday afternoon.

item.title: James Trafford says he left Man City for his 'mental wellbeing'
item.description: James Trafford has admitted that he joined Leeds in the summer for his own “mental wellbeing” after a lack of game time at Manchester City left him feeling “horrendous” last season. Academy graduate Trafford rejoined City in the summer of 2025 following a two-year spell at Burnley, but saw his ambitions of becoming the club’s number one dashed when Gianluigi Donnarumma came through the door from Paris Saint-Germain in the same transfer window. Having started the opening three games of the Premier League season prior to Donnarumma’s deadline-day arrival, Trafford was subsequently relegated to second choice, with Pep Guardiola mostly deploying him in cup competitions. He made just one more league appearance in the 35 matches that followed, which came on the final day of the season in City’s 2-1 defeat at home to Aston Villa , when Arsenal had already sealed the title. "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling, not playing," Trafford told BBC Sport . "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up. I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny. "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing. Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous. "I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve." James Trafford struggled for minutes at Man City (Action Images via Reuters) Trafford nevertheless played a significant part in City’s silverware successes last season, starting between the sticks for both the Carabao Cup final triumph against Arsenal and FA Cup final win over Chelsea at Wembley. His performances did enough to earn a place in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the World Cup that summer, serving as back-up to Jordan Pickford, with Trafford completing his £45m switch to Leeds after the tournament. Despite his struggles during his City return, Trafford does take value from that year of his career. "Going into any season, I always have the highest of hopes and always the belief that it will go the best way it could," he added. "Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens. Trafford started both of City's victorious finals at Wembley last term (Getty) "In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year. "There were moments when I was very down, regretting things and feeling disappointed, but looking back, I'm very thankful for the experience. What an incredible year."

item.title: Adam Scott reveals what players who have just left LIV Golf should be made to do now
item.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Adam Scott is a consummate professional in every sense. When numerous big-name players who were on the wrong side of 40 left the PGA Tour to join LIV Golf four years ago, Scott was tipped to follow them. After Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter, and Sergio Garcia all jumped ship from the PGA Tour, the spotlight was shining brightly on Adam Scott. However, Scott didn’t budge. He remained loyal to the PGA Tour and, by doing so, cemented his legacy as one of the game’s greatest golfers, but he also ensured he will end up on the right side of history. Now the Australian is adamant that those who played on LIV Golf should not be given a straightforward route back to the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour. Adam Scott demands former LIV golfers face a tough route back It was announced on Thursday that LIV Golf had officially folded as a business. LIV made some players wealthy beyond their wildest dreams, but the money they received obviously did not come without risk or consequence. Ben Parsons of Today’s Golfer asked Scott what he believes should happen now with the players who have just left LIV Golf. “ I mean, I think the fairest thing is that they all re-establish themselves in the system that they want to go to, whether that’s DP World or the PGA Tour, they left and gave up those privileges, “ the 46-year-old replied. “ So, you know, I think they should re-qualify themselves ideally. That’s how I would see it. I think that seems logical and sensible. “ Scott was then asked whether he thinks it’s a good thing that the best players in the world could soon be back playing together again. “ Hopefully that’s the case, yeah, “ the Australian replied. “ I mean, I think what we’ve seen with it all is, there’s probably enough events, and we have to find the right balance that everyone is kind of satisfied with guys being together enough, but there’s still enough interest and pathways and creating new talent and all this. “ And I think, you know, I think the last few years have shown us we all need to work towards making this, you know, a healthy sport and something that people get excited for. “

item.title: Heat Must Stop Making Excuses And Start Playing Hard
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are in trouble, and the players are finally admitting the hard truth. After a 138-117 loss to the Lakers on Monday and a loss to the Warriors on Thursday, the team sits at a disappointing 3-6 record. Opponents are scoring 123.9 points per game against them, which is the fourth-worst mark in the entire NBA. The defense has completely fallen apart, allowing teams to shoot 48.8% from the floor. That number is the third-worst in the league. It is time to stop pretending this is just a rough start and call it what it is: a failure to compete. Giannis Calls Out the Effort Problem Giannis Antetokounmpo did not sugarcoat the situation after the loss. He scored 30 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, but he knows the team effort is missing. “We’re not playing hard enough,” Antetokounmpo said, according to Field Level Media . He went on to explain that the squad lacks trust and needs to hold each other accountable on defense. Klay Thompson added 19 points and Bam Adebayo chipped in 16, but those individual numbers do not matter if the unit cannot stop the other team from scoring at will. The Heat have lost five of their first seven games, and the pattern is clear. Fatigue Is No Excuse for Bad Habits Bam Adebayo pointed to tired legs as a major cause of the breakdown. He noted that communication stops when players get worn down, leading to costly errors. “A lot of times I feel like when fatigue sets in, we stop communicating, and that’s when mistakes happen,” Adebayo said. He warned that these lapses allow bad habits to take root. The team needs to figure it out before the season slips away completely. Miami will try to reset on Wednesday night against the struggling Los Angeles Clippers in Inglewood. The Clippers are also in a mess, sitting at 1-6 after a six-game losing streak. Brandon Ingram, the Clippers’ leading scorer, is sidelined by a heel injury. Bradley Beal is also out with a knee issue. Despite the injuries, the Clippers managed to get a career-high 26 points from Kobe Sanders in their last loss. Max Strus made his debut with 11 points and offered a hopeful message about the team’s future. “Find ways to win, find ways to battle, consistently and down the stretch and we’ll get that with this group,” Strus said. He believes the squad is eager to learn and improve. Both teams are dealing with roster upheaval, but the Heat have a chance to prove they can bounce back. Giannis is listed as probable to play despite a minor wrist injury. Myron Gardner is questionable with a quad contusion. The Clippers hope to get Ingram and Yanic Konan Niederhauser back soon, but they are not there yet.

item.description: Leeds United v Brentford - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford has broken his silence on a testing period at Manchester City, describing the lack of regular playing time at the Etihad Stadium as a "horrendous feeling." The England international returned to his boyhood club with high hopes, only to find himself sidelined following a high-profile transfer window move. Sidelined at the Etihad Trafford progressed through the youth ranks at Manchester City before embarking on loan spells with Accrington Stanley and Bolton Wanderers. He eventually secured a permanent switch to Burnley, where a successful two-year stint prompted the Etihad giants to bring him back last summer. The shot-stopper anticipated becoming Pep Guardiola's first-choice goalkeeper upon his return. However, those ambitions were quickly derailed when Italy international Gianluigi Donnarumma arrived in Manchester on deadline day . The late signing relegated Trafford to the bench for almost the entire domestic campaign. He was completely frozen out of Premier League action from late August until Guardiola handed him a rare start against Aston Villa on the final day of the season. 'You just lose yourself' The lack of match action took a heavy mental toll on the goalkeeper. Speaking to BBC Sport , Trafford did not hold back when reflecting on his struggles. "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing," Trafford admitted. "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up. That frustration ultimately drove his summer departure to Elland Road . The Leeds number one stressed that consistent minutes were essential for his health and ambitions. "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing," Trafford explained. item.description: Kalyn Ponga featured with a protective arm guard for New Zealand [Getty Images] New Zealand (12) 34 Tries: Nikora, Gagai, McLean, Hughes, Willison, Nicoll-Klokstad Goals: Isaako 5 Tonga (10) 10 Tries: Fifita 2 Goals: Katoa Just 23 days after breaking his arm, Kalyn Ponga returned to inspire New Zealand to a 34-10 victory in a pulsating encounter with Tonga as they reached their first World Cup final since 2013. Ponga had been named initially in reserve and then as one of the interchange players in the build-up to this contest - and the expectation was that he would be eased back into action and play a limited role. Instead, head coach Stacey Jones stunned many with his decision to include Ponga in New Zealand's starting 13 but was repaid in full as the Newcastle Knights talisman starred on home turf at the McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, Ponga's impact from full-back was almost immediate as he sent Briton Nikora over in the right corner inside four minutes. He was also involved in the Kiwis' second try of the game - as his contest with his opposite number Lehi Hopoate was crucial to Dane Gagai grounding the ball. And while the swirling wind made conditions almost unplayable at times, he repeatedly gathered high kicks and made several telling defensive contributions. One of those included throwing himself in the way of Tonga's juggernaut second row Demitric Vaimauga to prevent a certain try, while his ability to stall Hopoate's run and prevent him from offloading to Isaiya Katoa stopped another at a key stage with New Zealand only 12-10 ahead. The prelude to this fixture was almost every bit as gripping as the main event. Tonga's traditional war dance, the Sipi Tau, was met by New Zealand's Haka and a long stand-off between the players provided the perfect backdrop to a contest brimming with athleticism, power and superb ball-handling skills. For the second week running, Tonga fans turned out in force with the stands a sea of red. And they witnessed their side's participation in a wonderful advert for rugby league with Jojo Fifita scoring two excellent tries. However, the match ultimately swung away from them in a five-minute period after the break when New Zealand's outstanding centre Casey McLean surged over in the left corner and the wily Jahrome Hughes darted in to score. On this occasion, Kristian Woolf's team, who effectively torpedoed England's hopes of reaching the last four with a 30-12 in their opening match on 17 October, were unable to stage the same sort of fightback that helped them defeat their Pacific Island rivals Samoa last weekend. With the scoreboard, time and a gale-force wind against Tonga, Xavier Willison punished them further when they failed to gather a short drop out. And when Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad superbly grounded Erin Clark's kick, it put the gloss on a fine New Zealand performance. item.title: 'What more do you want him to prove?': Ravi Shastri questions selectors over Mohammed Shami's retirement
item.description: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri is disappointed that Mohammed Shami did not get another chance in India's Test team before announcing his retirement from the format. Shastri believes the senior fast bowler had done enough to prove his fitness through his performances in domestic cricket. He pointed out that Shami regularly played for Bengal and bowled long spells despite questions about his fitness. Shastri said playing in the gym and bowling in an actual match were two different things. According to him, a bowler's ability to bowl 10-12 overs in a match should be a better test of fitness. “What's the point of being fit in the gym if you can't bowl 10 or 12 overs in a match? Here, you've got a workhorse who's bowling for you. So, I'm a little disappointed that he didn't get another go,” Shastri said on Sony Sports Network ahead of the second ODI. The former India coach also questioned what more Shami needed to do to convince the selectors that he was ready to play international cricket. 'What more do you want a player to do?' Shastri said Shami's regular appearances for Bengal and his bowling workload in first-class cricket were clear signs of his fitness. “I've heard all these press reports about his fitness not being good, but he was playing every game for Bengal. He was bowling 15-20 overs. What more do you want a player to do to prove his fitness? If he's in good form and has a good IPL, and one of your senior bowlers suddenly breaks down, you'll be looking for experience. But you've got a player like him there. “It's sad when someone who's played so well for the country has to go. I definitely thought he had another 30 or 40 wickets in him. He should have played in the last 12 months and perhaps should have been in the side as a Test-match bowler,” Shastri added. Shami played three Ranji Trophy matches for Bengal in the ongoing season and picked up 14 wickets. Shastri felt the experienced fast bowler could still have played an important role in India's Test attack.
